items.title: From 400 miles above Earth, AI tracks invasive leafy spurge
items.excerpt: Harnessing satellite imagery, AI deep-learning models and community science data, scientists from the University of Minnesota have tracked the spread of leafy spurge over a 20-year period.

items.title: Dark matter–hunting satellite Euclid reveals record number of cosmic 'magnifying glasses'
items.excerpt: UBC researchers have helped uncover 15,000 new potential strong gravitational lenses—the largest collection of these cosmic tools that help astronomers investigate dark matter.

items.title: AI and experiments reveal impurities hindering waste plastic pyrolysis oil recycling
items.excerpt: A Korean research team has identified how impurities interfere with the use of waste plastic pyrolysis oil as a petrochemical feedstock through catalytic experiments and artificial intelligence (AI)-based computational chemistry. The findings, published in the journal ACS Catalysis, provide a scientific basis for predicting potential declines in catalytic performance according to the types and concentrations of impurities present.

items.title: Less data, faster discovery: Researchers rethink AI's role in developing new materials
items.excerpt: Developing new materials often starts with understanding their electronic structure, or how electrons are arranged and behave within them. Calculating these electronic structures typically requires expensive simulations on supercomputers. That's led researchers to train artificial intelligence models on millions of simulated data points to make faster predictions.

items.title: Quantum neural networks with high-dimensional quantum neurons
items.excerpt: How can we scale up a quantum neural network? One way is to add more qubits as neurons. But a study titled "Quantum neural network equipped with backpropagation on a qudit processor" published in National Science Review shows another way.

items.title: AI toolbox accelerates bioreactor simulations by up to 10,000 times
items.excerpt: The control of large-scale industrial bioreactors is one of the most complex tasks in the process industry. In the often huge plants, the smallest differences in temperature, pH value or oxygen content determine the success or failure of a process.

items.title: Scientists who use AI propose less distinctive ideas for federal research grants
items.excerpt: A new study of U.S. federal grant applications suggests that scientists using generative AI tend to pitch research closer to previously funded topics. At the NIH, AI-heavy proposals won funding more often and preceded modestly more routine papers.

items.title: Scientists might have discovered what makes AI so effective at chess
items.excerpt: AI’s comfort with complexity could be key to its chess-playing prowess

items.title: AI has put young mathematicians in an impossible situation
items.excerpt: A survey of 268 graduate students and postdocs reveals researchers are unsure of their future in mathematics and uneasy about using AI—the very technology they fear

items.title: Using AI to accelerate neuroscience research
items.excerpt: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into neuroscience is changing how scientists engage with data, improving our understanding of the brain and leading to better ways of training computational models. The findings will be presented at Neuroscience 2026, the annual meeting of the Society for Neuroscience.
